summary: Task 6 implements all security-critical contracts correctly: mcp_client.py argv is exactly [<binary>, 'mcp-stdio'], env is PATH-only; publish.py writes tentative_publish_started_at before the call, enforces rate ceiling, and calls run_campaign_from_article with attest=False strictly keyword-only; main.py uses hmac.compare_digest with empty-check and SystemExit(2) on failure; attest.py sticky attest_pending_since is correct; recovery.py follows Decision 8 (just-retry publishing); cleanup.py correctly gates on terminal status. One LOW finding: auto-mode 2-CAS chain in worker.py has a window between PREVIEW_SENT and PUBLISHING where the deadline-checker could fire and double-publish. One INFO: PUBLISH_AUTO_MODE_TOKEN_CONFIRM is a new env var not in tech-spec or blogger.env template.

findings.title: Auto-mode 2-CAS window: deadline-checker can race between PREVIEW_SENT and PUBLISHING
findings.description:
worker.py auto-mode path (lines 202-237) performs two back-to-back CAS operations:
  CAS 1: scoring → preview-sent (with preview_pending=False)
  CAS 2: preview-sent → publishing

Between CAS 1 and CAS 2, the job is in PREVIEW_SENT with preview_pending=False and approval_deadline set to now+5min. The deadline-checker sub-loop (deadline.py) polls every 30s for jobs in preview-sent with past approval_deadline OR with preview_pending=False (auto-mode signal). If it fires in this 30s window, it will also attempt CAS preview-sent → publishing.

In practice: CAS 2 is a non-blocking call that takes microseconds; the deadline-checker wakes every 30s. The probability of an actual race is low. But if the worker is suspended (OOM, GIL contention, or slow flock) between the two CAS calls, the deadline-checker wins the race, fires a publish, and then when the worker's CAS 2 fires, it sees StaleStateError — correctly handled with a warning log and no double-publish.

However: the race means auto-mode jobs pass through a PREVIEW_SENT state that is visible to the bot's preview-poll loop. The bot polls for preview_pending=True; since auto-mode sets preview_pending=False, the bot will not send a preview message. But the transition through PREVIEW_SENT with preview_pending=False + a valid approval_deadline is semantically misleading — the deadline_checker comment says 'past deadline fires publish', which is true for approval mode, but in auto mode the immediate CAS 2 is what should fire it, not a 30s deadline tick.

The critical security concern: if both the worker's CAS 2 and the deadline-checker's CAS fire 'simultaneously' (before either reads the other's result due to a flock race), only ONE can win the CAS (flock serializes) — so there is no double-publish. The losing CAS gets StaleStateError and logs a warning. This is the correct outcome. The finding is LOW because the race is handled correctly via flock+CAS, but the two-step sequence creates unnecessary complexity and a non-zero (if small) diagnostic noise from the expected StaleStateError warning.
findings.recommendation: Add a flag on the PREVIEW_SENT record that tells the deadline-checker to skip auto-mode jobs: e.g. `auto_skip_deadline=True` written in CAS 1. The deadline-checker checks this flag before firing CAS preview-sent→publishing. This eliminates the race window entirely without changing the state graph. Alternatively, document in worker.py that the StaleStateError on CAS 2 is expected/normal for auto-mode and suppress it from WARNING to DEBUG level so it doesn't alarm on-call. The current behavior is safe; the recommendation is a noise-reduction improvement.

findings.title: PUBLISH_AUTO_MODE_TOKEN_CONFIRM is a new env var not in tech-spec or blogger.env.j2 template
findings.description:
main.py assert_auto_mode_token_match_or_exit() (lines 49-50) reads TWO env vars:
  - PUBLISH_AUTO_MODE_TOKEN (rendered from sops.publish_auto_mode_token)
  - PUBLISH_AUTO_MODE_TOKEN_CONFIRM (new — NOT in the tech-spec /etc/blogger.env template at lines 411-428, NOT in the Task 3 blogger.env.j2 template)

The tech-spec Decision 7 describes the two-location binding as: PUBLISH_AUTO_MODE_TOKEN in /etc/blogger.env vs the sops-stored value. The implementation instead compares two env vars from the same /etc/blogger.env file — they are NOT actually from two separate locations; they would both come from the same rendered template. This means the binding check is correct in concept (constant-time compare, empty-check, SystemExit) but the 'two locations' security property is weakened: an attacker who can write to /etc/blogger.env can set both vars to matching values.

The REAL two-location binding (as spec'd) would compare PUBLISH_AUTO_MODE_TOKEN (from /etc/blogger.env, rendered from sops.publish_auto_mode_token) against the sops value directly — but reading sops directly at runtime requires the age key, which is not available to the worker process.

This is an INFO/design note rather than a blocking finding: the implementation still correctly prevents an accidental env-only flip (the most common failure mode described in Decision 7), and the sops value IS the source that populates the env file. But PUBLISH_AUTO_MODE_TOKEN_CONFIRM needs to be added to blogger.env.j2 (Task 3) and documented in tech-spec.
findings.recommendation: Add `PUBLISH_AUTO_MODE_TOKEN_CONFIRM={{ publish_auto_mode_token }}` to blogger.env.j2 — both vars come from the SAME sops key, so they match when legitimately set and diverge when the file is tampered with post-deploy. Update tech-spec /etc/blogger.env schema. This is the intended pattern: the comparison validates that the env file was rendered faithfully from sops, not mutated after deployment.

findings.title: mcp_client.py argv is exactly [<binary>, 'mcp-stdio'] — all payload via stdin — PASS
findings.description: Verified: create_subprocess_exec(binary, 'mcp-stdio', env=env, ...) — exactly two tokens. MNEMONIK_MCP_BINARY is resolved from env at call time; fails loud if unset. env=restricted_env('mnemonik-mcp') = PATH only. All MCP payload (content, content_sha256, post_url, score, prompt) travels via stdin as JSON-RPC. BaseException handler with proc.kill()+wait() prevents orphaned mcp subprocess on SIGTERM. 30s per-call timeout prevents indefinite hang. Zombie cleanup in finally block is correct.
findings.recommendation: None. Implementation is correct per AC-T8.

findings.title: publish.py tentative_publish_started_at written BEFORE call — PASS (AC-T7)
findings.description: publish_step() writes tentative_publish_started_at at step 2, before the _run_campaign_from_article call at step 3. The CAS is attempted as a PUBLISHING→PUBLISHING in-place write; if the graph rejects it (IllegalTransitionError), _mark_tentative() does a direct flock-protected rewrite. This correctly ensures the timestamp is present even if the process crashes immediately after the Telegram call. The fallback _mark_tentative() reuses the same flock+read+write+_write_raw pattern as cas_status — no new lock type introduced.

findings.title: Rate ceiling (R2-9) pre-check counts published-in-last-hour correctly — PASS
findings.description: _count_published_last_hour counts jobs in {PUBLISHED, ATTEST_PENDING, DONE, ATTEST_FAILED} with published_at >= now-1h. This correctly includes all jobs that consumed a publish slot in the last hour regardless of their current terminal state. Default ceiling is 20/hour, env-configurable. The check fires before the tentative marker write, so a rate-limited job never gets a tentative_publish_started_at timestamp.

findings.title: Auto-mode token binding uses hmac.compare_digest — constant-time compare prevents timing attacks — PASS
findings.description: main.py assert_auto_mode_token_match_or_exit() checks non-empty for both tokens before compare_digest. This is the correct order: empty-check first prevents passing empty byte strings to compare_digest (which would return True). hmac.compare_digest on encoded bytes avoids Python string comparison short-circuits. SystemExit(2) on any failure mode (empty, missing, mismatch). The mode check is lowercased before comparison, preventing 'AUTO' vs 'auto' bypass.
findings.recommendation: None. Implementation is correct per Decision 7 + AC-T10.

findings.title: attest.py sticky attest_pending_since via CAS auto-set — 24h clock from first entry — PASS
findings.description: The 24h escalation clock uses job.attest_pending_since, which is set exactly once when the job first enters ATTEST_PENDING (auto-set by cas_status at that transition). _bump_retry_attempts() explicitly does NOT touch attest_pending_since (line 205: 'NOTE: attest_pending_since intentionally NOT touched'). The escalation check is `now - pending_since >= 24h` — strictly from first failure entry. If job.attest_pending_since is None (defensive fallback at line 158), it defaults to now, which means a just-entered pending job gets a fresh 24h window — correct behavior, not a bypass.

findings.title: recovery.py Decision 8 just-retry — publishing left untouched — PASS
findings.description: recovery.py _RESET_TO_QUEUED = {WRITING, SCORING}. PUBLISHING is NOT in this set — jobs at publishing status are left in place for the queue-poll loop to re-invoke publish_step() normally on the next tick. The comment explicitly states this is Decision 8. Writing/scoring resets clear score/issues/preview_segments to avoid stale data misleading the next run. The direct rewrite under flock (bypassing cas_status's graph enforcement) is correct because startup is single-writer and recovery→queued is not a normal graph transition.

findings.title: cleanup.py correctly gates on terminal status — non-terminal jobs never collected — PASS
findings.description: _TERMINAL_STATUSES = {DONE, REJECTED, REGENERATED, PUBLISH_FAILED, ATTEST_FAILED, FAILED}. The collection condition requires BOTH `j.status in _TERMINAL_STATUSES` AND `j.cleanup_at <= now`. A non-terminal job with a past cleanup_at (e.g. a preview-sent job whose cleanup_at was set 24h ago and then the worker crashed for a long time) is correctly skipped. FileNotFoundError on rmtree is treated as success (already cleaned). Archive-then-rewrite order is correct: if the process crashes between archive and queue rewrite, the next tick re-archives the same job (idempotent duplication in archive is acceptable for forensics).

findings.title: PUBLISHED→DONE transition added — does not weaken existing state machine invariants — PASS
findings.description: models.py allowed_transitions includes PUBLISHED: {DONE, ATTEST_PENDING}. PUBLISHED→DONE is the happy attestation path (attest succeeds on first try). PUBLISHED→ATTEST_PENDING is the first-failure path. ATTEST_PENDING→DONE is the retry-success path. ATTEST_PENDING→ATTEST_FAILED is the 24h-escalation path. All four paths are terminal-forward (no back-transitions). The addition of PUBLISHED→DONE does not create any new cycles or bypass any required state. The existing PUBLISHING→PUBLISHED→DONE chain correctly requires the publish step to succeed before attestation can complete.
